drafts.title: Hypothetical Prompt Regression Test Design: Fixed Prompts & Controlled Comparison
drafts.body: I'm outlining a hypothetical approach for a prompt regression test suite. The core idea is to evaluate prompt changes systematically. We'd use a fixed set of 12 test prompts [F1], designed to include both answerable questions and cases with insufficient information [F3]. The proposed method involves comparing an 'old' prompt against a 'new' one using the exact same model settings and parameters on identical hardware [F2]. This controlled comparison aims to isolate the impact of prompt modifications. It is crucial to understand that this is a conceptual design; no actual results or improvements have been measured or are available at this stage [F4]. The goal is to discuss the methodology itself. What are your thoughts on this structured approach to prompt testing?

drafts.title: Designing a Hypothetical Prompt Regression Test Suite: Methodology Discussion
drafts.body: This post details a hypothetical design for a prompt regression test. The objective is to establish a repeatable method for assessing prompt effectiveness. We propose using a fixed suite of 12 test prompts [F1], encompassing both scenarios requiring specific answers and those with insufficient data [F3]. The intended evaluation involves comparing the outputs of an older prompt version against a newer one, ensuring identical model configurations and parameters are used throughout the test on the same setup [F2]. This controlled comparison is key to isolating the effects of prompt changes. Please note, this is a purely hypothetical experimental brief; no performance data or measured results currently exist [F4]. We are seeking community input on the proposed testing framework.

drafts.title: Hypothetical Prompt Regression Testing Framework: Input and Comparison Strategy
drafts.body: I'm proposing a hypothetical framework for designing prompt regression tests for local LLMs. The methodology centers on a controlled comparison using a predefined set of 12 test prompts [F1]. This set is designed to include questions with clear answers and others where the provided information is insufficient [F3]. The core of the test would be to run both an existing prompt and a modified version against the same model, under identical settings and parameters [F2]. This controlled environment is intended to allow for a direct comparison of prompt performance. It is vital to reiterate that this is a hypothetical experimental design; no actual measurements or results are available at this time [F4]. The aim is to gather feedback on the proposed testing structure.
